In [[mathematics]], an element ''a'' of a [[commutative ring]] ''R'' is called '''(relatively) prime''' to an [[ideal of a ring|ideal]] ''I'' if whenever ''ab'' is an element of ''I'' then ''b'' is also an element of ''I''.

A proper [[Ideal (ring theory)|ideal]] ''I'' of a [[commutative ring]] ''A'' is said to be '''primal''' if the elements that are not prime to it form an ideal.
